stem: Meena's father wants to replace the old electrical wiring in their house in Jaipur. He asks Meena which property a metal must have so that it can be drawn into thin wires for the wiring. Which property should Meena name?

options.text: Ductility — copper and aluminium can be drawn into wires, so they are suitable
Shininess — any shiny material, even shiny coal, can be drawn into wires
Hardness — any hard solid can be made into wire if enough force is used
Brittleness — sulfur can be drawn into wires because it breaks easily

teacher.key_rationale: Ductility is the property that allows a material to be drawn into wires; metals such as copper, aluminium and steel possess it, while coal and sulfur are non-ductile and unsuitable. Options B, C and D each assert an incorrect property (shininess, hardness under force, brittleness) as the basis for wire-drawing. Key recalculated for the new item.
